content.text:
Best DX: make execution tools headless and presentation explicit.

```text
search_sdk / query_sdk / run_sdk
        ↓
structured data for the model — no iframe
        ↓
render_lobu_view only when a visual result helps
        ↓
one intentional card
```

Recommended contract:

- `run_sdk`, `query_sdk`, `search_memory`, etc.: no MCP App metadata. ChatGPT consumes their structured results internally.
- `render_lobu_view`: the single presentation tool, called once with final selected content.
- `resolve_lobu_approval`: remains app-only because it requires human interaction.
- Keep the view schema closed and deliberate: `text`, `code`, `table`, `diff`, `form`, `actions`.
- Delete the generic `UndeclaredResult`/`N fields` path. Raw technical payloads remain available in ChatGPT’s native tool-call inspector.
- Generate the app resource URI from the bundle hash instead of manually maintaining `v12`, `v13`, etc.

This produces:

- Zero repeated “Completed / 4 fields” cards during internal work.
- One useful card when there is genuinely something to inspect or act upon.
- No model-dependent return-shape tricks such as requiring `rows`.
- No growing zoo of `isCommandResult`, `isEntityResult`, `isBrowserResult`, etc.
- The same headless contract works in ChatGPT, Codex, Claude and other MCP clients.

I would not start by adding a special successful-command renderer. That fixes this screenshot but preserves the underlying universal-renderer complexity. The clean change is to stop attaching a UI to arbitrary power-tool results.

This alters MCP tool presentation metadata, and adding a `table` block would extend the public view contract, so I’d surface the exact contract diff for confirmation before implementation.

No—I said it too broadly. We still put relevant data in the App. We stop automatically mounting an App for every raw tool result.

There are two different cases:

| Case | What the user sees | What is persisted |
|---|---|---|
| Agent saves ordinary memory | Native message: “Saved X to memory” | Memory event immediately |
| Agent creates an approval interaction | Interactive approval card with exact proposal/form/diff | Pending run + approval event |
| User approves | Card becomes “Approved” and inert | Operation executes; decision/result events persist |
| User rejects | Card becomes “Rejected” | Rejection persists; operation does not execute |

### Existing approval flow

This part already works:

```text
Agent requests governed operation
        ↓
Lobu stores pending run + approval event
        ↓
Agent calls render_lobu_view(run_id)
        ↓
App displays exact proposal, form, Approve/Reject
        ↓
User clicks
        ↓
resolve_lobu_approval
        ↓
Server revalidates user + org + session + event version + expiry
        ↓
Canonical operation handler approves/rejects
```

The approval card is server-authored from the durable event—not invented by the model. The hidden capability is session-bound and short-lived. That is implemented in [mcp_app.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/mcp_app.ts:505).

So the data is absolutely inside the approval App. What disappears is the useless intermediate card:

```text
Completed
└── 4 fields
```

### If you mean approving the memory write itself

That is a real current gap.

Today, `save_memory` commits immediately and returns a receipt. It is explicitly configured as “write without confirmation” and also automatically attaches the generic App, producing the screenshot you saw: [registry.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:268).

The repository already documents the missing workflow: stage → review diff → commit/discard in [knowledge-as-git.md](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/docs/plans/knowledge-as-git.md:215).

The best DX would be:

```text
Explicit “remember this”
→ save immediately
→ no widget
→ assistant confirms naturally

Agent-inferred or “show me before saving”
→ stage memory proposal
→ interactive card shows text, type, entities, superseded fact
→ user edits and approves/rejects
→ only approval appends the final memory event
```

That avoids asking twice when the user already explicitly requested the save, while preserving review when the agent inferred something.

### Required code changes

1. Remove automatic UI metadata from ordinary `search_memory`, `save_memory`, `query_sdk`, `query_sql`, and `run_sdk` results.
2. Keep UI metadata on `render_lobu_view` and approval-only helpers.
3. Reuse the existing runs/events approval primitive for reviewed memory proposals—no new database table.
4. Add a clear staged-write contract, probably a separate `propose_memory` tool rather than overloading `save_memory`.
5. Keep widget state presentation-only; the authoritative proposal and decision stay server-side.
6. Verify ChatGPT does not add an unwanted second host confirmation after the in-card Approve click.

This matches OpenAI’s recommended [decoupled data/render pattern](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui#separate-data-processing-from-ui-rendering): data tools return `structuredContent`; only an intentional render tool mounts the widget. The widget can then invoke approval tools and retain local UI state through the documented [component bridge](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/reference#capabilities).

I have not changed the code—the staged memory-write tool would be an MCP contract change and needs your confirmation first.

For a complex mixed read/write script, `run_sdk` should remain headless. The UX should be “plan → approve → commit → summarize,” with an App only for the approval step.

This is an interactive-decoupled flow.

### When the user already explicitly authorized it

```text
User: “Clean up these duplicate memories.”
        ↓
run_sdk executes
        ↓
Agent receives structured result
        ↓
Assistant: “Scanned 1,842 memories. Created 8, superseded 24,
left 1,810 unchanged, and encountered no failures.”
```

No iframe unless a table, diff, or links would materially help.

The structured result might be:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "dry_run": false,
  "return_value": {
    "scanned": 1842,
    "created": 8,
    "superseded": 24,
    "unchanged": 1810,
    "failed": 0,
    "sample": [
      {
        "old_event_id": 481,
        "new_event_id": 912,
        "title": "Updated deployment preference"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The agent still receives all this through `structuredContent`; removing the widget metadata does not remove the result data. That emission happens independently in [mcp-handler.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:521).

### When the changes need review

Do not let one opaque script read, decide, write, and only then explain itself. Split it:

```text
1. Plan
   Read memory and calculate an exact change set.
   Write nothing.

2. Review App
   Show the selected changes and consequences.

3. Commit
   Apply that exact approved change set.

4. Result
   Update the same App or give a native summary.
```

The card should look approximately like:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Review memory cleanup                       │
│                                             │
│ Scanned                         1,842        │
│ New memories                         8       │
│ Existing facts to supersede          24      │
│ Unchanged                         1,810       │
│                                             │
│ ▸ Review 32 proposed changes                │
│                                             │
│ [Reject]                 [Approve 32 changes]│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

After approval, the same card becomes inert:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Memory cleanup completed                    │
│                                             │
│ 32 changes applied · 0 failed               │
│ 8 created · 24 superseded                   │
│                                             │
│ [Open memory]  [View audit]                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Critical safety property

Approval must bind to the exact proposed change set—not merely rerun the original arbitrary script.

The proposal should capture:

- Script/change-set hash
- Organization and approving user
- Existing event IDs expected to be current
- Exact new content
- `supersedes_event_id` mappings
- Stable idempotency keys
- Expiry/version token

At commit time, Lobu revalidates those conditions. If memory changed since preview, it returns “proposal is stale” instead of silently applying something different.

Current `run_sdk(dry_run=true)` is useful for inspecting skipped writes, but it is not sufficient for this guarantee: skipped handlers do not execute, and later script logic may depend on their outputs. Complex reviewed work therefore needs a real plan/commit boundary.

### Current implementation gap

Today:

- `run_sdk` returns the necessary structured execution envelope.
- It automatically attaches the generic App, causing `Completed → 4 fields`: [registry.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:320).
- `dry_run` returns side-effect previews.
- There is no signed “approve this exact `run_sdk` plan” continuation.

So the simplification is:

1. Remove automatic UI from `run_sdk`.
2. Keep its structured result.
3. For straightforward authorized runs, summarize natively.
4. For reviewed runs, introduce a durable plan/commit workflow using the existing approval machinery.
5. Let the approval widget call the commit tool and update itself without remounting.

That follows OpenAI’s recommended [decoupled data/render pattern](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui#separate-data-processing-from-ui-rendering).

### Codebase simplification

Today, [result-view.tsx](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/owletto/src/mcp-apps/interaction/result-view.tsx:1643) is 2,011 lines and guesses whether arbitrary output is SQL, SDK data, an event, a receipt, or a declared template. Its own comment identifies ordering hazards caused by this guessing.

The simplified architecture becomes:

```text
Data/execution tools — no UI
├── search_memory
├── save_memory
├── query_sdk
├── query_sql
└── run_sdk

Explicit presentation tool
└── render_lobu_view
    ├── saved_event(event_id)
    ├── review_approval(run_id)
    └── render(blocks)
```

That lets us remove:

- Automatic shape detectors and precedence rules
- Generic `Completed → N fields` fallbacks
- Tool-specific rendering branches
- Much of the snapshot/restoration complexity for ordinary calls
- Many combinations currently covered by the enormous generic-host test matrix

We keep:

- Approval/forms
- JSON-template rendering
- Charts, metrics, tables, markdown and links
- Secure host-mediated actions
- Widget state for filters and disclosure

So there is a real net simplification after the old path is deleted. During migration, while both paths coexist, it will temporarily be larger.

### Single-event embedded dashboards

Yes. One durable report event can contain the complete dashboard snapshot:

```json

  "title": "Weekly product report",
  "semantic_type": "report",
  "payload_type": "json_template",
  "payload_template": {
    "root": {
      "type": "card",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "columns",
          "children": [
            {
              "type": "metric",
              "label": "Signups",
              "value": "{{signups}}"
            },
            {
              "type": "metric",
              "label": "Active users",
              "value": "{{active_users}}"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "line-chart",
          "data": "{{daily_users}}",
          "xLabel": "Day",
          "yLabel": "Users"
        },
        {
          "type": "bar-chart",
          "data": "{{sources}}"
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "data": "{{incidents}}"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "payload_data": {
    "signups": 84,
    "active_users": 312,
    "daily_users": [],
    "sources": [],
    "incidents": []
  }
}
```

The existing event model already preserves that template and its typed data. There is already integration coverage for a stored bar-chart event in [notify-kind-payload.test.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/notifications/notify-kind-payload.test.ts:223).

The ChatGPT renderer already supports:

- Bar, line and area charts
- Pie charts
- Stacked-area charts
- Sparklines
- Metrics and tables

Those are implemented in [json-template-view.tsx](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/owletto/src/mcp-apps/interaction/json-template-view.tsx:1214).

### Expected flow

```text
User: “Create my weekly dashboard”
        ↓
run_sdk computes the report
        ↓
save_memory writes one json_template report event
        ↓
returns event_id: 493
        ↓
render_lobu_view({ action: "saved_event", event_id: 493 })
        ↓
ChatGPT embeds that saved event as a dashboard
```

The render call would not create a duplicate report. It would permission-check and read event `493`, then transport it as:

- `structuredContent`: concise model-visible summary, event ID and version
- `_meta`: complete template and larger chart datasets for the widget

This follows OpenAI’s [decoupled data/render pattern](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui#separate-data-processing-from-ui-rendering).

The same durable event can therefore render in:

- ChatGPT as an embedded dashboard
- Lobu’s Activity/event UI
- Other MCP Apps-compatible clients
- Text-only clients as a summary plus authoritative link

### Snapshot versus live dashboard

A single event is ideal for a report snapshot: reproducible, shareable and auditable.

For interactivity:

- Local filters, tabs and chart selection use widget state—no new event.
- Opening links requires no new event.
- Refreshing the underlying report creates a new event that supersedes the old one.
- Actions that change workspace or external state go through governed tools/approval.

Because Lobu events are append-only, we should never mutate the original dashboard event in place.

The one missing piece is the explicit `saved_event(event_id)` rendering variant. Currently, dashboards render only because the generic result renderer happens to recognize the template triple. Adding the explicit variant is a small MCP contract change, but it lets us safely delete far more generic code while retaining the dashboard capability.

Yes — I’m now highly confident the better boundary is: **don’t render `run_sdk`; render intentional user experiences.**

Official OpenAI guidance explicitly warns that attaching a widget to every tool call remounts the iframe too often. It recommends data/action tools returning normal results and a separate render tool owning `_meta.ui.resourceUri`. [OpenAI’s decoupled UI guidance](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui#separate-data-processing-from-ui-rendering)

What popular servers do:

- **Playwright MCP:** ordinary browser tools returning snapshots, text, screenshots, and files. No universal MCP App around every operation. [Source](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp)
- **Context7:** two focused retrieval tools returning model-consumable documentation, without custom UI. [Source](https://github.com/upstash/context7)
- **Notion’s public MCP server:** 22 search/read/write tools, again without a universal result widget. [Source](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server)
- **GitHub MCP is the strongest comparison:** I counted 116 tool snapshots, but its UI build enumerates only four Apps: identity, issue writing, PR creation, and PR editing. [Tool inventory](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/tree/main/pkg/github/__toolsnaps__), [UI apps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/github-mcp-server/main/ui/scripts/build.mjs)

GitHub’s approval behavior is especially relevant: write forms appear only when the host supports MCP Apps, execution pauses, and the operation runs after the UI resubmits it. UI helper tools are hidden from the model. [Form deferral logic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/github-mcp-server/main/pkg/github/ui_capability.go), [app-only helper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/github-mcp-server/main/pkg/github/ui_tools.go)

For Lobu, I’d use this boundary:

```text
run_sdk / query_sdk / query_sql / memory operations
    → compact native tool result
    → no Lobu iframe

render_lobu_view(event_id)
    → dashboard, chart, report, editor, approval
    → Lobu iframe appears once
```

A report still works as one durable event:

```text
run_sdk
  ├─ reads memory
  ├─ writes one report event containing the dashboard/view specification
  └─ returns event_id

render_lobu_view(event_id)
  └─ embeds that saved dashboard in ChatGPT
```

The render call does not need to write another data event. It simply presents the already-persisted event. Charts, tables, filters, and drill-down controls can all live in that single saved report event.

For approvals:

```text
run_sdk → { status: "needs_approval", approval_event_id }
render_lobu_view(approval_event_id) → interactive approval
user submits → approved action executes → event is superseded/completed
```

One nuance: ChatGPT may still show its native collapsed “tool completed” trace. Lobu cannot necessarily remove that host-level disclosure. What we can remove is the useless custom `Completed → 4 fields` iframe.

So the concrete recommendation is:

- Remove rich-result MCP metadata from `run_sdk`, queries, and ordinary memory tools.
- Keep `render_lobu_view` as the deliberate UI boundary.
- Potentially add a purpose-built approval tool later, following GitHub’s pattern.
- Keep every underlying tool functional in clients that do not support MCP Apps.

That gives cleaner chat UX, fewer iframe mounts, simpler result-shape code, portable tools, and rich dashboards exactly when the user actually asked to see something.
